tagline: A loop around the Elkhorns through the old gold towns.
intro: From Baker City, once called the Queen City of the Mines, OR 7 heads south and then west up the Powder River to Phillips Lake, and on past fields of dredge tailings to Sumpter. The road climbs over Blue Springs Summit to Granite, turns north on Forest Road 73, tops out among the peaks above the Anthony Lakes and comes down abruptly into the Baker Valley at Haines.
Along Granite Creek, watch for rock walls left by Chinese miners, who set the bigger boulders aside as they worked the creek for gold.
season: TripCheck gives summer and fall as the best time to visit.

moments.title: Sumpter
moments.text: The boom town of three newspapers and an opera house lost 12 blocks to fire in 1917, fought partly with dynamite, and dredged its valley for gold until 1954.

moments.title: Granite
moments.text: When the War Production Board shut down gold mining in 1942, Granite went from 86 people in 1940 to two in 1960.

moments.title: Elkhorn Summit
moments.text: The loop tops out at 7,392 feet among the jagged peaks behind the Anthony Lakes, where skiers have been coming downhill since 1933.

practical: Between Granite and Anthony Lake the road is often closed by snow until July, and there are no services between Granite and Baker City.
